title: Microsoft 365 admin center: Organizational messages now supports hybrid-joined devices
summary: Hold: the Windows delivery automation creates a policy object but does not configure the delivery setting it claims to control. The Intune navigation also omits the Create step that opens the configuration wizard. The roadmap facts, device requirements and stated licence requirements are supported.

claims.claim: Recipients of Windows-channel messages need Windows 11, version 25H2 or 24H2 Enterprise.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn gives no hybrid-specific configuration or separate admin switch, and its Devices requirement only names supported device types.
claims.quote: Searched: "organizational messages" "hybrid" configuration unmanaged devices license. Read the organizational-messages-microsoft-365 page and FAQ in full; their Windows configuration is general and the Devices bullet only lists the two join types.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the arrival default for the hybrid-joined support change.
claims.quote: Searched: "organizational messages" "hybrid" "default". Read roadmap description, organizational-messages-microsoft-365 and its FAQ; none states how this support expansion affects existing delivery on arrival.

claims.claim: No source says that hybrid-joined support changes existing message behaviour.
claims.quote: Searched: "organizational messages" "hybrid" "default", and organizational messages hybrid joined devices default automatic existing messages configuration unmanaged prerequisites licenses pricing meter. Read roadmap, main Learn page and FAQ; no existing-message transition is stated.

claims.quote: In the Assignments page, select the groups that should be targeted by this policy and then select Next. Include any users or devices that might receive organizational messages.

claims.claim: Messages contain text and links chosen by the organisation.
claims.quote: Customize: Add customization to the message including full text and custom URLs.

claims.claim: Device restriction policies that block the listed Windows Spotlight or Windows Tips settings can block organisational messages.
claims.quote: ensure that none of the following settings are set to Block: Windows Spotlight. Windows Spotlight on lock screen. Windows Tips. Windows Spotlight in action center. Windows Spotlight personalization.

claims.quote: Make sure Disable Cloud Optimized Content is set to Disabled.

claims.claim: Windows delivers organisational messages on a pull model.
claims.quote: Windows delivers messages on a pull model, so the system buffers messages on a set period for each of the channels.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Windows messages might take 24 or more hours to arrive, so the suggested test allows at least 24 hours.
claims.quote: Since devices might be configured to request content at different times, messages might take 24 or more hours before the message is received and rendered.

claims.claim: The organisational messages Learn page describes no meter, Copilot Credits consumption or separate charge for the feature.
claims.quote: Searched: "organizational messages" pricing meter credits licensing. Read organizational-messages-microsoft-365 and its FAQ in full; both describe licence requirements but neither publishes a meter, credit rate or separate charge.

claims.where: licensing notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Advanced customised creation and aggregate targeting require the tenant to have at least one Microsoft 365 E3/E5, Office 365 E3/E5 or Windows Enterprise E3/E5 licence.
claims.quote: Admins and users can access these advanced features for organizational messages when the tenant has at least one of the following licenses: Microsoft 365 E3, or E5 license. Office 365 E3 or Office 365 E5 license. Windows Enterprise E3 or E5 license.

claims.claim: Windows custom messages require Windows E3/E5 or Microsoft 365 E3/E5.
claims.quote: Windows custom messages require Windows E3 or E5, or Microsoft 365 E3, or E5.

claims.claim: Teams custom messages require Office 365 E3/E5 or Microsoft 365 E3/E5.
claims.quote: Microsoft Teams custom messages require Office 365 E3 or Office 365 E5, or Microsoft 365 E3 or Microsoft 365 E5.

claims.claim: Pre-made messages might still be available without the listed custom-message licences.
claims.quote: Pre-made messages might still be available without these licenses.

claims.claim: Usage targeting includes Microsoft Copilot-licensed users who have not recently used Copilot.
claims.quote: Inactive Copilot users: all users with a Microsoft Copilot license that have not used Copilot in the prior 28 days.

claims.claim: The cited pages publish no licence requirement specific to hybrid-joined devices.
claims.quote: Searched: "organizational messages" "hybrid" configuration unmanaged devices license; "organizational messages" pricing meter credits licensing. Read organizational-messages-microsoft-365 and FAQ; licence passages do not distinguish device join types.

claims.claim: Recipients need access to the Microsoft products the messages are configured for.
claims.quote: Recipients must have access to the Microsoft products the messages are configured for delivery.

claims.claim: Recipients do not need Microsoft Entra roles to receive messages.
claims.quote: end users aren't required to have any Microsoft Entra roles to receive organizational messages.

claims.claim: The Windows tenant-policy requirements do not apply to sending Teams notifications or email messages.
claims.quote: Set tenant policies only if you need to deliver messages to Windows surfaces such as Windows Spotlight, Windows Notification Center, and Windows Taskbar. You don't need to set tenant policies for sending messages to Teams Teaching notifications or to Email.

claims.claim: Teams notification channels support recipient selection only through Microsoft Entra groups.
claims.quote: Teams notification channels only support recipient selection via Microsoft Entra groups.

claims.claim: Tenants that have not scheduled a message in the past 30 days can need additional initialisation time.
claims.quote: the organizational messages system might take up to 24 to 48 hours to initialize for tenants where a message wasn't scheduled in the past 30 days.

claims.claim: Review activity reports Messages seen, Clicks and Dismisses.
claims.quote: The Review activity page opens where you can review insights data for your messages including: Three time-series data charts showing daily changes in the total Messages seen. Total Clicks. Total Dismisses.

claims.claim: Learn does not explain how hybrid-joined devices that are not Intune-managed should be configured for delivery.
claims.quote: Searched: "organizational messages" "hybrid" configuration unmanaged devices license. Read organizational-messages-microsoft-365 and FAQ; they give Intune policy steps but no handling of unmanaged hybrid-joined recipients.

claims.claim: The printed Intune route goes from Settings catalog directly to Configuration settings and then to Enable delivery of organizational messages (User).
claims.quote: Under Profile type, select Settings catalog. Select Create. The Create profile wizard opens.
claims.fix: Replace the path with 'Devices > Manage devices > Configuration > Policies > Create > New Policy > Windows 10 and later > Settings catalog > Create > Configuration settings > Add settings > Experience > Enable delivery of organizational messages (User)'. The second Create opens the wizard, as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/admin/misc/organizational-messages-microsoft-365.

claims.claim: POST /beta/deviceManagement/configurationPolicies is the automation equivalent for enabling Windows organisational-message delivery.
claims.quote: Create a new deviceManagementConfigurationPolicy object. In the request body, supply a JSON representation for the deviceManagementConfigurationPolicy object.
claims.fix: Set controls[0].api to null and remove its Graph-create explanation from the row note and Governance controls prose. The cited operation creates the policy container; its documented request properties do not set Enable delivery of organizational messages (User), so it is not the equivalent delivery control.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 admin center role-assignment path reaches Organizational Messages Writer through Users, Active users and Manage roles.
claims.quote: From the left navigation bar, select ... Show all, and then select Users to expand it. Under Users, select Active users.
claims.fix: Use the full documented path 'Show all > Users > Active users > user > Manage roles > Admin center access > Show all by category > Other > Organizational Messages Writer'. The omitted Show all is the navigation-expansion step; the remaining printed labels match https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/admin/misc/organizational-messages-microsoft-365-faq.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments assigns an Entra role using principalId, roleDefinitionId and directoryScopeId.
claims.quote:
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments
{"@odata.type": "#microsoft.graph.unifiedRoleAssignment", "principalId": "<Object ID of user or group>", "roleDefinitionId": "<ID of role definition>", "directoryScopeId": "/"}

claims.claim: The mixed licensing notes distinguish licensed advanced/custom features from pre-made messages that might be available without those licences.
claims.quote: Windows custom messages require Windows E3 or E5, or Microsoft 365 E3, or E5. Microsoft Teams custom messages require Office 365 E3 or Office 365 E5, or Microsoft 365 E3 or Microsoft 365 E5. Pre-made messages might still be available without these licenses.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout and After rollout
claims.claim: Every control the governance checklist asks the reader to check or configure has a controls-table row.
claims.quote: Checklist: Check that no Intune device restriction policy sets ... to Block; Open the two Windows delivery endpoints; Review Messages seen, Clicks and Dismisses. Table: Windows delivery setting, author/approver roles, and stopping/removing messages only.
claims.fix: Remove the checklist bullets beginning 'Check that no Intune device restriction policy', 'Open the two Windows delivery endpoints', and 'Review Messages seen, Clicks and Dismisses'. Their factual explanations can remain in the body; these checklist controls have no corresponding table rows. Do not add rows as part of this correction.
